cases.answer: In the cited meta-analysis of 30 NSCLC studies (n = 3,287), sensitivity was similar for tumor-informed and tumor-agnostic assays at the landmark timepoint (42% vs 44%) and at the longitudinal timepoint (76% vs 79%). Tumor-informed assays had higher specificity at both timepoints: landmark 97% vs 93%, and longitudinal 96% vs 88%.

cases.answer: Compared with chemotherapy alone, single ICI significantly increased the risk of any cardiac adverse event (RR 2.15; 95% CI 1.13–4.12; p = 0.02; I2 = 0%; 9 trials, 6,929 patients; evidence quality low). Single ICI plus chemotherapy also significantly increased the risk (RR 1.38; 95% CI 1.05–1.82; p = 0.02; 12 trials, 6,391 patients; evidence quality high). The increase was larger for single ICI alone than for ICI plus chemotherapy.

cases.answer: The review cites a meta-analysis of 26 studies. The pooled CSF ctDNA detection rate was 86% (95% CI 79%–91%), which is the proportion of cases in which ctDNA was detected. Separately, pooled sensitivity was 91.8% and pooled specificity 93.5% for detecting CNS metastases in NSCLC. Individual study detection rates ranged from 82% to 100%. CSF cytology detected 60% (95% CI 36%–81%), so ctDNA detection was significantly higher.

cases.answer: No. The review says no MCED test has shown a mortality benefit to date. It also says no blood-based screening strategy has demonstrated a mortality benefit. By contrast, LDCT has a demonstrated lung-cancer mortality benefit, and the review cites the NLST for this. The NHS-Galleri trial increased early-stage detection but missed its primary endpoint.

cases.answer: Among US women aged 50–64, cervical-only screening was 27.1% and CRC-only screening was 5.4%. The authors say cervical-only screening was about five times as common as CRC-only screening (27.1/5.4 ≈ 5.0).

cases.ambiguity: Subgroup ratios differ (for example 36.8% vs 6.9% in one subgroup), but the overall figure is about five-fold.

cases.answer: The consensus says reflex testing in early-stage, resectable disease is now also vital. The ADAURA data show adjuvant therapy applies even to stage 1b disease, so EGFR mutations should be sought as early as possible. That means in the resected tumour or, ideally, in presurgical specimens if available. Targeted therapies are also now becoming established in the neoadjuvant setting.

claims.claim: Reflex testing in early-stage resectable disease is vital, because ADAURA shows adjuvant therapy applies even in stage 1b, so EGFR should be tested early, and targeted therapy is becoming established in the neoadjuvant setting.
